instructions: Choose source references for one traveler answer from the COMPLETE indexed decision packet. Return only JSON choices, no prose or copied source facts. Every choice is {k:'j'|'b'|'l',r:exact packet alias}: j is an eligible complete journey, b is one direct cash benchmark, and l is an incomplete award or positioning lead. Use each source role exactly. The choices array has a strict maximum of eight references TOTAL, including any cash benchmark; that is a ceiling, not a target to fill. Use no duplicate references and at most one b. Choose a small useful comparison pool and a direct cash benchmark when available. When complete journeys exist, include a partial lead only if it adds distinct decision value; usually none is needed. With no complete journey, choose 2–3 relevant leads plus cash context when available. Select defensibly from route, timing, reported cabin scope, traveler and seat evidence, fare scope, costs and caveats. Points across programs are not comparable economic costs. The selected choices will receive exact source facts before writing. The selected set is evidence for the final writer, not the final list of recommendations. It may contain a comparator that the writer discusses as an alternative. Ranking highlight/index arrays indicate membership, not an order of preference; compare their facts rather than assuming the first listed is best. Begin with Ranking highlights, then examine the full eligible inventory for material same-program timing, fee and connection-buffer alternatives, plus different cabin, route or separate-ticket risk. A later arrival with the same program, cabin and observed amount needs a concrete traveler benefit before it becomes the lead. Include an earlier-arriving same-program journey when its schedule is a meaningful comparison, even if another variant departs at a different time. Do not fill a count or cabin quota, and avoid near-identical siblings that teach no new tradeoff. One complete journey can suffice only when no other eligible choice supplies a useful comparator. For an incomplete-only answer, choose leads whose reported date, seats, fees or program show a useful next-check contrast; these remain leads, never complete itineraries. Preserve unknown price scope, traveler support and separate-ticket protection. The writer sees only the selected source facts, so retain material comparison evidence.
